The attacker's code then runs as root, according to advisories that Debian, Ubuntu, and APT's developers published on November 4. item.title: Critical Rails Flaw Lets Attackers Write Server Files via Crafted ImageMagick Uploads
item.description: A critical flaw in Ruby on Rails could allow an unauthenticated attacker to write arbitrary files on an app's server by uploading a crafted file if the app processes uploads using ImageMagick. The Rails project disclosed the flaw in an advisory and fixed it in versions 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2. The flaw is in Active Storage, the part of Rails that handles file uploads. Some apps store…

item.title: Xen Hypervisor Flaws Let One Malicious VM Read and Write Any Other VM's Memory
item.description: Two flaws in the Xen hypervisor allow a malicious guest virtual machine (VM) to read and write the memory of other VMs on the same host, including dom0. Dom0 is the VM that, by default, has full permissions and manages the others. Patches are out, and there is no known mitigation, the Xen Project said in an advisory on November 3. All Xen versions from 4.6 onward are vulnerable…

item.title: Radio With No Radar: Why Agent Runtime Security Fails Without the Layers Beneath It
item.description: Nearly every agent security pitch now ends on the same promise: the product stops the bad action in real time.
